# Inspector

In **Unity 6**, public fields work directly. Private fields use Unity's normal `[SerializeField]`. No companion initial-value field, linking attribute, or `Awake` is needed.

| Mode | What you can do                                                          |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Edit | Set initial values, save scenes/prefabs, and use Undo.                   |
| Play | View and edit current values. Changes are discarded when Play mode ends. |

For runtime-only component fields, use `[System.NonSerialized]`. For custom Inspector value structs, add `[System.Serializable]` and follow Unity serialization rules. Unity 2022.3 uses the optional `[MaskedValueField]` bridge instead of automatic fields.

Unity 6 initial values remain plaintext configuration in memory and assets. Loading or cloning restores those defaults, not current gameplay state. `[NonSerialized]` is a serialization setting, not memory protection.

See the package's detailed [Inspector guide](https://github.com/achieveonepark/masked-value/blob/main/Documentation~/Inspector.md) for the Unity 2022.3 example, assembly references, codec-backed fields, and additional serialization details. Browse the [Inspector Fields sample](https://github.com/achieveonepark/masked-value/tree/main/Samples~/InspectorFields) for a working Unity 6 example.

# Performance and limits

Unmanaged value reads, writes, and remasking allocate no managed memory after initialization. String reads and assignments and custom codecs can allocate; larger structs also cost more memory and processing. Synchronize concurrent access yourself.

`GuardedValue<T>` adds integrity checks to the masked value path. Choose it for unmanaged values that need those checks; use `MaskedValue<T>` when masking without integrity checks is sufficient. `RefreshMask()` is explicit and is not required on each read.

Masking is not encryption or complete anti-cheat protection. Code patches, valid snapshot replay, and legitimate API writes remain possible. Unity 6 initial values remain plaintext configuration in memory and assets; loading or cloning restores defaults, not current gameplay values. `[NonSerialized]` does not provide memory protection.

These are package-level characteristics, not a guarantee of zero overhead on every target. Measure the application's access patterns and target devices. For benchmark methodology and implementation details, see the [package performance notes](https://github.com/achieveonepark/masked-value/blob/main/Documentation~/Performance.md).

# Samples and AI coding tools

## Samples

Import samples from **Package Manager > Masked Values > Samples**:

- **Class Fields** — runtime fields, guarded health, strings, structs, and a custom codec.
- **Inspector Fields** — Unity 6 fields for health, speed, position, player name, and custom stats. Add `InspectorFieldsExample` to a GameObject.

## Use with AI coding tools

Copy the included `Skills~/achieve-masked-values` folder into your project's `.agents/skills/` for Codex or `.claude/skills/` for Claude Code. Unity Skill Manager can collect the packaged skill for you.

- **Codex:** `$achieve-masked-values`
- **Claude Code:** `/achieve-masked-values`

The [package skill](https://github.com/achieveonepark/masked-value/blob/main/Skills~/achieve-masked-values/SKILL.md) guides field setup, Inspector use, memory and serialization limits, and a tamper listener that stops gameplay and requests shutdown on detection.

# Tampering

`GuardedValue<T>` refuses to return or overwrite a value when its integrity check fails. `.Value` and `RefreshMask()` throw `InvalidOperationException`; `TryGetValue`, `TrySetValue`, `CheckIntegrity`, and `TryRefreshMask` return `false`. Stop the current game action on failure and do not use failed output as valid state.

## Respond to detection

Subscribe to `GuardedValueDiagnostics.TamperingDetected` to respond. It reports the value type on the checking thread, **when the next check fails**, rather than at the exact external memory write. An unused value is not checked automatically; call `CheckIntegrity()` at a suitable interval for important values you do not otherwise access.

The package does not shut down the game automatically. To stop gameplay and request shutdown once on the main thread, connect the [ready-to-use Unity listener](https://github.com/achieveonepark/masked-value/blob/main/Documentation~/Tampering.md#unity-listener-quit-on-detection). It signals a thread-safe flag; in the Editor it stops Play mode. Follow the [full tampering guide](https://github.com/achieveonepark/masked-value/blob/main/Documentation~/Tampering.md) for lifecycle and failure-handling details.

## Protection limits

Masking and lightweight integrity checks are not encryption or complete anti-cheat protection. Code patches, valid snapshot replay, and legitimate API writes remain possible. Keep authoritative online game state on the server.

# Types and operations

## Choose a type

| Type              | When to use it                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GuardedValue<T>` | Health, currency, or other unmanaged values that need masking and tamper detection.               |
| `MaskedValue<T>`  | Numbers, enums, or unmanaged structs that need masking without integrity checks.                  |
| `MaskedString`    | Strings. Use `ValueEquals` to compare or `CopyTo` to read into a reusable buffer.                 |
| `MaskedData<T>`   | Data containing references; supply an explicit `ISpanValueCodec<T>`. See the Class Fields sample. |

`MaskedValue<T>`, `MaskedString`, and `MaskedData<T>` do not provide integrity detection. Use `GuardedValue<T>` for unmanaged values whose corruption should trigger a response.

## Read, write, and calculate

```csharp
using Achieve.MaskedValues;

GuardedValue<int> health = 100;
health -= 10;
health += 5;
health *= 2;
health /= 2;
int currentHealth = health;       // Implicit read, with integrity validation.
health.Value = 80;                // Explicit write, also validated.
bool isAlive = health > 0;
```

Numeric wrappers also support `%`, `%=`, unary signs, and `++`/`--`. Results retain the wrapper type: `var result = health + 10` is a `GuardedValue<int>`. Use `int result = health + 10` or `health.Value + 10` for a plain number.

Integer addition, subtraction, and multiplication wrap on overflow, including inside a caller's `checked` block. Use `.Value` when you need the underlying type's own arithmetic rules or custom struct operations.

`GuardedValue<T>.RefreshMask()` changes the masked representation while keeping the value. Call it explicitly when needed; reads already validate integrity.

See the [Inspector guide](/masked-value/guide/inspector.md) for field setup and [tampering guide](/masked-value/guide/tampering.md) for failure handling.

# Masked Values

Mask gameplay values in memory and detect ordinary memory tampering with `GuardedValue<T>`. The package supports numbers, unmanaged structs, strings, and data with custom codecs. It supports **Unity 2022.3 and later**, with automatic Inspector support in **Unity 6**, and has no external package dependencies.

Masking makes simple plaintext searches harder; it is not encryption or complete anti-cheat protection. Keep authoritative online game state on the server.

## Installation

### Git URL

In **Window > Package Manager**, select **+ > Add package from git URL** and enter:

```text
https://github.com/achieveonepark/masked-value.git#v1.0.1
```

### OpenUPM

With the [OpenUPM CLI](https://openupm.com/docs/getting-started-cli.html), run this from your Unity project folder:

```sh
openupm add com.achieve.masked-values
```

To install through a scoped registry instead, merge these entries into `Packages/manifest.json`, preserving any existing registries and dependencies:

```json
{
  "scopedRegistries": [
    {
      "name": "OpenUPM",
      "url": "https://package.openupm.com",
      "scopes": ["com.achieve.masked-values"]
    }
  ],
  "dependencies": {
    "com.achieve.masked-values": "1.0.1"
  }
}
```

## Quick start

Add this component to a GameObject. In Unity 6, its fields also appear in the Inspector.

```csharp
using Achieve.MaskedValues;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class PlayerState : MonoBehaviour
{
    public GuardedValue<int> health = 100;
    public MaskedValue<float> moveSpeed = 5f;
    public MaskedString playerName = "Player";

    public void TakeDamage(int amount) => health -= amount;
}
```

Choose a [value type](/masked-value/guide/types-and-operations.md) based on whether integrity checks and custom codecs are needed. See the [Inspector guide](/masked-value/guide/inspector.md) for Unity field behavior and [tampering guide](/masked-value/guide/tampering.md) for handling failed integrity checks.
